To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GRB hosts have star formation rates that are 10-100 times higher than previously thought, and that the star-forming galaxies that host GRBs are representative of the star-forming population as a whole.

about 20 % of GRB host have star formation rates that exceed 500 M☖ yr-1, and the remaining hosts have a star-formation rate of about 50 M☖ yr -1 (5 σ), and that GRB hosts, as a group, have bluer R - K colors than galaxies selected in the radio and submillimeter.
GRB host galaxies, as a whole and individually, are more representative star-forming galaxies compared with those uncovered in submillimeter and/or radio blank surveys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the starburst properties of gamma-ray burst (GRB) host galaxies and their relationship to the GRB phenomenon.
the study of the host galaxies in which gamma-ray bursts occur.
the detection and characterization of the host galaxies and the afterglows of gamma-ray bursts ( GRB s) in the radio and millimeter wavelength bands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the submillimeter observations of GRB host galaxy fields are an important and unique way of probing the star formation rate density of the universe, and they will be even more important in the near future.
GRB host galaxies represent the best laboratories to date for the study of dust-enshrouded starbursts.

we have detected the submillimeter emission from two GRB host galaxies and that the nondetected host galaxies have an average star formation rate of 100 M☖yr-1, a luminosity about 20% less than Arp 220 and R-K colors that are significantly bluer than submillimeter- or radio-selected galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GRBs are a valuable tool for studying star-forming galaxies at high redshifts, but the GRB hosts do not represent the most extreme cases.

the submillimeter/radio observations of GRB hosts are a glimpse into the future of star formation studies, where GRBs will serve as beacons for the discovery of the most luminous star-forming galaxies in the universe.
GRB hosts appear to be a representative sample of the star-forming population at high redshift.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GRB hosts have a higher star formation rate than other star-forming galaxies, which will make them a unique probe of the high-redshift universe.
the GRB hosts, as a whole, probe a population of star-formingers galaxies that is more representative of the star-forming galaxy population than that uncovered in blank submm and radio surveys.
the GRB hosts, as an ensemble, are representative of the local starburst population, and thus, they are a natural complement to blank submillimeter surveys.
